title: GW1 roundup
body:
*GAMEWEEK 1 — ROUNDUP*

———

*RESULTS*

Tom 29 – 52 Jack
Iain 48 – 46 Calum
Adam 17 – 57 Brian
Edmund 27 – 45 Giles

———

*STANDINGS*

1. Brian (Sesko Meal Deal) — 1-0-0, 3 pts (57 for)
2. Jack (The Beauties) — 1-0-0, 3 pts (52 for)
3. Iain (Marshmellow3.0) — 1-0-0, 3 pts (48 for)
4. Giles (Quantum of Tzolis) — 1-0-0, 3 pts (45 for)
5. Calum (Ndiaye Hart) — 0-0-1, 0 pts (46 for)
6. Tom (Lord Farsquaad) — 0-0-1, 0 pts (29 for)
7. Edmund (115 Love Notes XI) — 0-0-1, 0 pts (27 for)
8. Adam (Diomande Eyes XI) — 0-0-1, 0 pts (17 for)

———

*THE GAMES*

*Tom 29 – 52 Jack*
Jack by 23.
Tom: led by Raya (6), Havertz (6), Wilson (3); 2 left on the bench, Roefs the pick of them.
Jack: led by João Pedro (11), Dewsbury-Hall (11), Guéhi (10); 1 blank (Muñoz); 14 left on the bench, Tavernier the pick of them.
Tom's Lord Farsquaad side never got out of first gear, with Raya and Havertz both stuck on 6 and Wilson chipping in a modest 3. Jack's Beautiful Boys were altogether more comfortable, João Pedro and Dewsbury-Hall both hitting 11 while Guéhi added 10, leaving a bench of 14 largely academic. Tom will want to know why Roefs was left warming the pine while Raya laboured.

*Iain 48 – 46 Calum*
Iain by 2.
Iain: led by Xhaka (9), Gvardiol (9), Pickford (7); 14 left on the bench, Trafford the pick of them.
Calum: led by Calafiori (9), Cherki (8), Tzolis (6); 2 left on the bench, Sels the pick of them.
A tight one at the top, settled by the narrowest of margins. Iain's Xhaka and Gvardiol both weighed in with 9 apiece and Pickford's 7 proved just enough, while Calum's Calafiori matched the best of them with 9 but Tzolis's 6 wasn't quite sufficient to close the gap. Two points, decided perhaps by team selection rather than talent.

*Adam 17 – 57 Brian*
Brian by 40 — never in doubt.
Adam: led by Rice (3), Tielemans (2), Scott (2); 2 blanks (James, Kerkez); 6 left on the bench, Verbruggen the pick of them.
Brian: led by Palmer (13), White (11), Saka (9); 2 blanks (Frimpong, Marmoush).
Adam's Diomande Eyes never threatened, with Rice's 3 the high point of a limp scoreline further hampered by blanks from James and Kerkez. Brian's Sesko Meal Deal were ruthless by comparison, Palmer's 13 and White's 11 doing the heavy lifting as Saka chipped in 9, making this one look over before it started.

*Edmund 27 – 45 Giles*
Giles by 18.
Edmund: led by Ødegaard (11), Gravenberch (5), Lewis-Skelly (3); 2 blanks (Cash, Thiago); 3 left on the bench, Leno the pick of them.
Giles: led by Gakpo (12), Szoboszlai (8), Rogers (8).
Edmund's 115 Love Notes leaned heavily on Ødegaard's 11, but with Gravenberch and Lewis-Skelly managing only 5 and 3 respectively, and blanks from Cash and Thiago, there wasn't enough support. Giles's Quantum of Tzolis were more evenly spread, Gakpo's 12 backed up by Szoboszlai and Rogers both hitting 8, enough to see this one home comfortably.

———

*STAR MAN* — Palmer (CHE), 13 pts, for Brian

*Top starters:* Palmer 13; Gakpo 12; Ødegaard 11; White 11; João Pedro 11

*Lowest starters:* Marmoush 0; Kerkez 0; James 0; Frimpong 0; Cash -1

*Points left on the bench*

Jack — 14
Iain — 14
Adam — 6
Edmund — 3
Tom — 2
Calum — 2
Giles — 0
Brian — 0

———

Four wins, four losses, and already a table that flatters no one equally.

Brian tops the pile on 57 without needing his bench, which feels unfair on the other seven.

Jack and Iain leave 14 apiece on the bench and still win; Giles and Brian leave none and also win, so no lesson there.

Cash goes to -1 for Edmund, a rare achievement in round one.

Bottom three separated by two points, which is either a tight league or a shallow one.
